# Design

Hypermid gives Gideon durable project knowledge, recoverable long conversations and supervised local capabilities through one versioned system. Raw history stays authoritative; context projections are derived; every model call and module effect retains identity and ownership.

A user continues a project across restarts and long sessions, sees what the agent remembers and why, recovers original evidence, controls background costs, and manages local modules through native Gideon interfaces.

Deliver context projection and recall, persistent knowledge and maintenance, shared storage and protocol foundations, process supervision and routing, event delivery, client SDKs, operator tooling and product surfaces.

The first complete vertical integration is Gideon OSS. A generic host adapter contract is included; additional agent-host adapters are not prerequisites for the Gideon release.

- Hosted control-plane changes or deployment
- Replacing Gideon's authoritative final-answer delivery
- Replacing provider authentication or approval policy
- Claims of unlimited active context or perfect recall

A Python package under runtime/gideon/hypermid adapts Gideon's existing runtime lifecycle. Rust crates under crates/hypermid-* implement bounded transport, deterministic projection, durable stores and supervised services. TypeScript, Rust, Python and Swift clients implement the same versioned contracts.

Gideon's journal owns original conversation events and final delivery. Hypermid owns derived projection state and its knowledge records. One context authority per session and one fenced mutation authority per project prevent duplicate compaction or maintenance.

Owner-scoped durable storage supports SQLite first and an explicit PostgreSQL backend contract. Multi-store effects use a persisted intent and reconciliation; cross-store operations never pretend to be one SQLite transaction.

Existing cognition, history, embeddings, permissions, MCP, lifecycle and console capabilities are inventoried before replacement. Existing records are migrated or adapted through source hashes and versioned checkpoints; no parallel hidden source of truth is introduced.

spec/hypermid/schemas/*.schema.json define Draft 2020-12 document shapes. Runtime authorization, cursor ordering, uniqueness across records, digest equality and transaction invariants are specified separately and cannot be established by JSON Schema alone.

Hypermid v1 uses a four-byte unsigned big-endian body length followed by a UTF-8 JSON envelope, capped at eight MiB. Larger logical data uses ordered chunks capped at 64 KiB. Unix sockets are local defaults; Windows uses authenticated loopback. Every application session uses TLS 1.3 mutual authentication and ordered per-session sequence numbers. Remote access requires explicit configuration, TLS and scoped principals.

Authenticated connection state determines the owner identity. Request scope is checked against that identity, not trusted as a grant. Background workers obey the same project write boundary as foreground tools.

schemas/common.schema.json is the only definition of Id, Scope, Digest, Cursor, Error and Trace. Other documents reference those types.

Opaque case-sensitive identifiers are bounded ASCII strings. Display paths and labels are not identities. Owner and project identities remain stable across allowed renames and aliases.

Every project operation carries owner_id and project_id; workspace_id is optional and never grants mutation authority by itself. Owner-wide operations require a separately authorized owner capability.

Cursor epoch is a positive integer and sequence a nonnegative integer, both bounded to the interoperable JSON safe-integer range. Sequence exhaustion rotates the epoch through an explicit durable transition rather than wrapping.

Digest is a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 over the explicitly defined byte encoding; each producing contract identifies its canonicalization rule.

Error code is stable and machine-readable, message is bounded/redacted, retryable does not imply safe effect replay. Unknown external-effect state requires reconciliation.

Every implementation wave closes with a Gideon consumer, durable state, observable output and a specified acceptance journey. Foundations are introduced alongside a consumer; no isolated crate milestone counts as product completion.

Requirements and tasks are normative in spec.kvx. Supporting design and schemas refine them; conflicts require an explicit spec revision before implementation. All implementation tasks begin pending.

Every mapped product capability has a requirement, an owning task, implementation paths and observable acceptance. Build-time support is classified explicitly. No capability is considered implemented because a design or schema exists.

Future verify_cmd entries are implementation acceptance commands, not evidence of execution. Document validation checks syntax, references, dependency order, coverage and schemas only.

Disabled, read-only shadow, project opt-in and default-on are separate durable configuration states. Shadow mode can compare projections but cannot publish facts, mutate the journal, issue duplicate maintenance calls or advance serving cursors.

A session changes context authority only at a quiescent turn boundary with a journal digest and migration checkpoint. Failed cutover retains the prior authority; resumed work reconciles the recorded intent.

Disable serving from the new projection while preserving original journals and accepted knowledge. Downgrade is allowed only across declared compatible schema versions; incompatible state requires a matching restore or forward repair.

Final release acceptance covers the entire capability map and the OSS installation/upgrade/user journeys; earlier vertical slices do not imply full-system completion.

Hypermid provides OSS-only shared Rust crates for canonical identity, fenced storage, cache policy, model and usage contracts, encrypted push, fleet logging, message buses, and role protocols, with typed Python adapters under runtime/gideon/hypermid.

Use common.schema.json Id, Scope, Digest, Cursor, Error, and Trace definitions. Canonical filesystem identity and transport binding generations remain distinct from those shared wire identities.

All 21 functional source crates are planned. Runner, compaction, and transform protocols are treated as alpha; compaction and transform require newly implemented live-route conformance suites before qualification.

First integration is open-source Gideon only. Hosted rollout, hosted migration, and hosted certification are excluded.

Hypermid is a local-first authenticated process fabric implemented in Rust and consumed by Gideon through a typed Python adapter. It owns module discovery, supervision, routing, flow control, durable effects, events, diagnostics, registry lifecycle, service integration, and optional federation.

spec/hypermid/design/context.txt

Hypermid owns immutable context state and deterministic projections behind a bounded versioned protocol; runtime/gideon/hypermid is the first adapter and Gideon remains the product authority for sessions, providers, tools, and authorization.

Hypermid memory is an OSS-only, source-grounded durable substrate backed by crates/hypermid-memory and integrated through runtime/gideon/hypermid. Authoritative revisions and mutation events are preserved; indexes, embeddings, summaries, and prompt projections are rebuildable.

Every mutation, including background maintenance, requires the actor Scope to own the target Scope or hold an unexpired grant for the exact operation. Process role, workspace membership, and maintenance status never confer write authority.

Use common.schema.json Id, Scope, Digest, Cursor, Error, and Trace definitions; do not create a second identity contract.

First integration targets OSS Gideon only. No hosted rollout, hosted migration, or hosted service is included.

Native OSS Gideon console, CLI, desktop, HostAdapter, and generic client experience for Hypermid administration and inspection. The Rust daemon/core remains authoritative and Gideon's Python adapter owns host translation. No duplicate standalone web UI and no hosted rollout.

Hypermid v1 uses a four-byte big-endian JSON length, an 8 MiB frame ceiling, ordered chunks no larger than 64 KiB, authenticated local Unix or Windows loopback transport, and explicit TLS opt-in for remote access.

Surfaces adopt authoritative cursors, expected digests, typed effect outcomes, and terminal receipts. HTTP completion, process exit, schema presence, optimistic state, or reconnect alone never proves a mutation committed.

Use Gideon's existing Settings, Diagnostics, Connections, terminal, shared headers, cards, forms, tables, dialogs, and responsive shell. Hypermid is one native destination with progressive disclosure, not a catch-all panel or separate web application.

Python is required for the Gideon HostAdapter. Rust, TypeScript, and Swift clients provide wire and outcome parity. Generic SDKs may ship in OSS; they do not imply hosted availability.

A full HostAdapter negotiates identity, scopes, sessions, memory, configuration, credentials, lifecycle, cursors, and reconnect. An MCP bridge exposes bounded tools only and is labeled separately.

Keyboard, touch, screen-reader, reduced-motion, focus, announcements, linear reading order, 44px targets, 320/390px layouts, and high-risk review flows are first-class acceptance criteria.

Hypermid has four principal integration components (foundation/contracts, context, memory, daemon/fabric) backed by the shared Rust workspace and integrated only through runtime/gideon/hypermid. Shared wire types come from hypermid-protocol and hypermid-contracts; Gideon retains ConversationLog, the model/tool loop, provider credentials, approvals, usage ledger, final response, delivery, and product surfaces.

The complete local daemon, adapter, migration, rollback, CLI, console, packaging, and conformance journey ships in OSS before any separate deployment work.

Wave 1 is authenticated local pass-through and status only. Gideon remains the sole default writer. Hypermid ownership is opt-in from wave 2 onward after a scoped barrier and writer lease.

Exactly one context writer exists for each owner/project/workspace scope. Shadow is read-only and cannot summarize, append, mutate memory, or update an index.

Raw Hypermid knowledge events are append-only and digest chained. Memory supersession, deletion, undo and rollback append new events. Gideon ConversationLog remains transcript authority, and derived summaries are admitted only against its covered source digest.

NativeAgentRuntime, ModelProvider, ToolCatalog, McpClientRegistry, ApprovalGate, ConversationDirectory, run_chat, ResultDelivery and UsageJournal retain their current authority.

ConversationDirectory remains the surface authority. Before daemon acceptance Python owns cancellation; after acceptance the daemon exclusively owns the request token and Rust children until it returns an effect-state receipt.

No provider, subscription, OAuth, MCP, channel or environment credential crosses the Hypermid protocol.

Handshake negotiation, N and N-1 protocol support, copy-validate-cutover migration, retained rollback checkpoints and unknown-effect reconciliation are mandatory.

Hypermid enforces scoped authority, encrypted daemon access, sandboxed effects, bounded network and model use, provenance-aware memory, verified artifacts, durable lifecycle controls, and crash recovery across crates/hypermid-*, runtime/gideon/hypermid, and native Gideon UI.

The OSS implementation and mandatory security gates are complete. Package qualification and remaining limitations are recorded in spec/hypermid/release-readiness.kvx; live-provider qualification remains an explicit opt-in gate.
